title: The Specimen Chip
summary: Round 2's 'Four numbers. One diagnosis.' layout comes back as it was, and the square of dots in the centre is replaced by a painted chip: a flat block of 100 where red paints the share of whichever number you pick, the number itself is printed into the block, and a small scale and one line of words say exactly what the 100 stands for.
story: After the reframe says most teams fix the wrong layer, this section brings in the market's own research as outside proof, paints each finding as a share you can see at a glance, and hands the letter its cue with 'Not one of them moves with more activity'.
motion: Standalone mockup: the head plays as usual. The plate's rules draw, the four readings come in with their numbers rising from below, and the four corner marks register. The chip then builds like a printed specimen: its pale ground paints down from the top, the scale's ticks calibrate from 0 up to 100, the figure 17 prints, and the red rises from the base to 17 (about 0.9s). The level stops partway up the printed 17, so its lower half turns paper on red. Cell 01 takes its rule as the red starts to rise.

The control is then demoed once: 95:5 at 2.55s, 77 at 3.4s, 53 at 4.25s and back to 17 at 5.1s. Each change is one slow, even morph (0.8s in the demo). The red level travels, the small marker on the scale rides with it and fills in when it lands, every scale tick the level passes turns dark, and the printed figure and the words underneath swap. Everything has settled by about 5.9s, and nothing moves after that.

Interaction: press a big number (anywhere on its reading works), or a button on the band, and the chip morphs to that reading in 1.1s. Hovering a number previews its reading in the chip, with a grey rule over that reading, and moving away returns the chip to the pressed one. The arrow keys move between the four numbers and select as they go. Home and End jump to the first and last. The numbers and the band buttons always agree.

On the live homepage the head plays as the section arrives. The plate and the chip wait until the plate is 40% on screen, then play the same build once, ending on 17. There is no automatic stepping on the live page, and nothing loops.
Reduced motion: the final state (17 shown, red at 17, marker filled), with no timers.
addressed: 'The previous design direction looked more proprietary … round two's design direction was good': round 2's layout is back exactly. That means the head, the four big numbers on the hairline cross with their labels and sources, the corner registration marks, the centre zone, and the FIG. 03 band with the 17% · 95:5 · 77% · 53% control.

'Change the kind of artifact … which was a square with dots … an information block or something painted in colors': the dots are gone. In their place is a painted block of 100, square and flat. Red paints the share, a pale ground holds the rest, and the reading's number is printed into the block like a Swiss poster.

'Equally proprietary, rather than just slapped in': the chip is built like a printed specimen rather than a chart. When the red sits below the printed figure (the 17), the level cuts through it, so the figure is half ink and half paper. There is a calibrated scale whose ticks turn dark as the level passes them, a marker that rides the level and locks when it lands, and a printed label strip naming the reading and what the full block stands for ('100 = the purchase').

It answers the numbers directly. Press or hover any big number, or use the band control, and the block re-proportions to that reading in one slow, mechanical move. Each reading names its own unit in words, using round 3's honest wording ('Share of the purchase spent with sales — every vendor combined'; '95 not buying · 5 buying now'; and so on). Only one reading is ever shown on the scale at a time.

Round 3's fixes are kept. The lede is 'Every one gets blamed on the pipeline. Not one of them moves with more activity.' Sources and wording are exactly as on the live site. The red is always the big number's own share, so 95:5 paints the 95. The field note 'The 17% window · 5 min' sits quietly in the band.
notes: Stage 1393px at 1440 (same as round-2 X). Layout is X's, unchanged: .ac-head (FIG. 03 meta kept, as in X); a 2×2 of 176px readings on cols 1–4 / 9–12 with the hairline cross; a 72px --panel caption band. Copy: the claims and so-lines are verbatim from StructuralEvidence.tsx, with em dashes and 'brand, product, and price'. X's comma edits are dropped, as in S. Numerals do not count up (round 3's integrity fix). CHIP: a 400×500 registration frame on the crossing, with a paper knock-out so the cross stops at the frame and four .ac-reg marks. The block is 100 units × 3px = 300×300. The ground is --panel with a 1px --line-2 keyline; red is --accent and paints from the base. One registered property (@property --km-evidence-V-v, a <number> from 0 to 1) drives the red field's height, the datum hairline and node position, and each tick's ink state (opacity clamp from the level minus the tick). A change of reading is therefore one CSS transition on that property (1100ms live, 800ms in the demo, --ease-inout). The printed figure (Mona wide 430, 104px) is set twice: ink on the ground, and paper inside the red field, which clips it (overflow hidden). That makes the level a real knock-out line through the figure. Red = the big numeral's share for every reading (17 · 95 · 77 · 53). Round 3's bar filled 5 for 95:5; here 95 is painted, so the red always matches the number pressed, and the unit line says '95 not buying · 5 buying now'. Strip (mono 12px, one line of 40 characters or fewer): 'R·0n · Name' with '100 = the purchase / your market / buyers / loyalty'. These are substrings of the unit wording, naming what the full block stands for, so the value is not repeated a third time. Scale labels 0 · 50 · 100 are 11px --fg-3 (calibration, not data). Controls: numeral <button aria-pressed> with a roving tabindex inside each cell (the cell is the hit area); the band .ac-seg buttons are aria-pressed and kept in sync. Hover preview uses a 90ms intent delay, mouse only. Readings stack in one grid cell, so nothing reflows. Entrance is keyed to .is-go, set by the JS; on html.km-home the plate is held (.is-wait) until the grid is 40% visible. Without JS nothing is held. Visible words at rest are about 145, over STORY's 120 cap, because X's layout (claims and so-lines in all four cells) is back by the founder's note. One more tension: STORY's D12 rationale said the reframe owns the page's only toggle. His round-4 note brings back round 2's band control here, so the page now has two (reframe and evidence). ≤760px: the readings sit in a 2×2 at 64px with the chip below at 2.4px per unit; strips and sources wrap; verified at 375px with no horizontal scroll. Mobile avoids display toggles on animated elements, because a viewport flip restarts their entrance.
